question: In square \(ABCD\), points \(E\) and \(F\) lie on \(BC\) and \(CD\), respectively, and \(\angle EAF=45^\circ\). How can you prove that \(EF=BE+DF\)?
solution: Half-angle model: Rotate \(\triangle ADF\) through \(90^\circ\) about \(A\) to obtain \(\triangle ABF'\). Then \(F'\), \(B\), and \(E\) are collinear. Since \(\angle EAF'=45^\circ=\angle EAF\) and \(AF=AF'\), we have \(\triangle AEF\cong\triangle AEF'\), so \(EF=EF'=BE+DF\).
